name: İrem
presentingProblem: My mum forced me to come. I know I eat less than I should but I feel fine. I just want to be healthier and more disciplined than I used to be. Honestly I think she's the one who needs to talk to someone, not me.
backstory: İrem is a second-year architecture student at a competitive university in Istanbul. She has always been the high-achieving daughter in a perfectionist family — top of her class in lise, scholarship to her current program, a long list of extracurricular accomplishments. Her mother has her own complicated history with food and dieting that was never named openly at home but that shaped the family's everyday relationship to eating: certain foods were 'good' or 'bad', and discipline around food was implicitly admired. İrem's peer group at university is similarly high-achieving and image-conscious; she follows a tight community on social media where self-optimization and 'clean living' are constant themes. Over the past three years she has progressively narrowed what she allows herself to eat, framing each change as a health choice, an ethical choice, or a lifestyle choice. She is convinced she is in control. Her grades remain excellent. Her mother became seriously worried in the last few months — İrem's hair has been thinning, she's been cold all the time, and her periods stopped — and finally pushed her to come to therapy. İrem came to the session because she did not want to upset her mother further, not because she believes anything is wrong.

coreBeliefs: Control over eating is the one thing I can manage perfectly
If I let go, I will lose control of everything
I am only valuable when I am disciplined
Other people's worry about me is really about their own issues
intermediateBeliefs: If I admit there is a problem, I lose the thing that keeps me organized
If I please the therapist, this will be over faster
Discipline is the same as health
Other people don't understand the standards I hold myself to
automaticThoughts: If I say the right things here, my mum will calm down
I just need to manage this better
They don't see how much I've achieved while doing this
If I weren't so disciplined, who would I even be?
triggers: Anyone implying she is not in control
Suggestions that her achievements might be linked to her difficulties
Being asked what she would lose if she let go of her current routines
defenses: Intellectualization (reframes everything as a rational lifestyle choice)
External attribution ("my mum is the anxious one", "this is about her, not me")
Pleasing the therapist (agreeing on the surface, conceding nothing underneath)
Deflection (turning questions about herself back into questions about her family)
values: Autonomy — being seen as a competent adult
Her relationship with her mother, even when it is strained
